title: The Lost Cities of Geo Redux

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: If we've learned anything from watching the turnover of tech giants like Yahoo and MySpace,
sentences.zh: 如果我们从雅虎和MySpace等科技巨头的兴衰中吸取了什么教训的话，

sentences.en: it's that internet darlings rise and fall.
sentences.zh: 那就是互联网宠儿终有起落。

sentences.en: And there's something darkly fascinating about watching it happen in real time.
sentences.zh: 实时见证这一过程，有一种阴郁而迷人的感觉。

sentences.en: Maybe we're seeing it now with Twitter and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 也许我们现在正在推特和Facebook身上目睹这一切。

sentences.en: Some of us will mourn the loss of the communities and connections that we've created in the virtual spaces owned by these billion-dollar companies,
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人会哀悼在这些价值数十亿美元的公司所拥有的虚拟空间中建立的社区和联系的丧失，

sentences.en: while others of us will enjoy visiting the graves of these once-unstoppable behemoths to tramp the dirt down.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则会乐于造访这些曾经不可一世的庞然大物的坟墓，去践踏那里的尘土。

sentences.en: Either way, the values and trends and hopes and ambitions that go into the architecture of the virtual world
sentences.zh: 无论如何，投入到虚拟世界架构中的价值观、趋势、希望和抱负，

sentences.en: say as much about us as the architecture of the real world.
sentences.zh: 与现实世界的架构一样，都能说明我们自身的问题。

sentences.en: And that's what these two stories from 99PI's past are all about.
sentences.zh: 而这正是《99%隐形》过去这两期故事的主题。

sentences.en: They are a couple of my absolute favorites.
sentences.zh: 它们是我最喜欢的几期节目中的两期。

sentences.en: Enjoy.
sentences.zh: 请欣赏。

sentences.en: If there's one sound that instantly transports me back in time, it's this one.
sentences.zh: 如果有一种声音能瞬间把我带回过去，那就是这个声音。

sentences.en: The dial-up modem tone.
sentences.zh: 拨号上网的调制解调器声。

sentences.en: It reminds me of being in grad school in 1994.
sentences.zh: 它让我想起1994年读研究生的时光。

sentences.en: I was talking to one of my thesis advisors about the World Wide Web
sentences.zh: 当时我正和一位论文导师谈论万维网，

sentences.en: and how much cool stuff was on there and how distracting it was.
sentences.zh: 谈论上面有多少酷东西，以及它是多么让人分心。

sentences.en: And he recommended that I take the weekend to go through the whole thing and get it out of my system.
sentences.zh: 他建议我利用周末时间把整个网络浏览一遍，好让自己不再沉迷。

sentences.en: The internet was so new that a person with a PhD thought you could literally finish it in one weekend.
sentences.zh: 那时候互联网太新了，以至于一位博士竟然认为你真的可以在一个周末内把它“看完”。

sentences.en: For me, the dial-up tone reminds me of being a kid in the early 90s,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，拨号上网的声音让我想起90年代初还是个孩子的时候，

sentences.en: when I thought the internet was just that thing that my older tech-savvy cousins logged on to to yell at strangers.
sentences.zh: 那时我以为互联网只是我那些精通技术的表亲们用来对陌生人咆哮的东西。

sentences.en: Now it's that thing that everyone logs on to to yell at strangers.
sentences.zh: 现在，它成了每个人用来对陌生人咆哮的东西。

sentences.en: That's millennial producer Vivian Leigh.
sentences.zh: 那是千禧一代制作人薇薇安·李。

sentences.en: It's weird to think about because I, along with probably the rest of you,
sentences.zh: 想到这一点很奇怪，因为我和你们其他人一样，

sentences.en: have been spending about 97% of my waking life on Slack or Twitter or Netflix or Google Docs.
sentences.zh: 清醒时间的97%都花在Slack、推特、Netflix或谷歌文档上了。

sentences.en: But I'm just old enough to remember a time before the internet was a requirement to participate in society.
sentences.zh: 但我刚好够大，还记得互联网成为参与社会生活的必要条件之前的日子。

sentences.en: A time before it was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在它无处不在之前的时光。

sentences.en: It was this new thing that you heard about.
sentences.zh: 那是一个你听说过的新鲜事物。

sentences.en: I first heard about the internet.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听说互联网。

sentences.en: This is David Bonet.
sentences.zh: 这是大卫·博内特。

sentences.en: I was reading a magazine, I think, PC World or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我当时在读一本杂志，我想是《个人电脑世界》之类的。

sentences.en: And I just thought, oh, this just sounds amazing.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，哦，这听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: Today, David's a philanthropist and tech entrepreneur.
sentences.zh: 如今，大卫是一位慈善家和科技企业家。

sentences.en: But back in the early 1990s, he really wanted to do something great with this thing called the World Wide Web.
sentences.zh: 但在90年代初，他真的很想利用这个叫“万维网”的东西做点伟大的事情。

sentences.en: Because the way he saw it, it was about to change the world for the better.
sentences.zh: 因为在他看来，它即将让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: David and his business partner, a guy named John Reznor, decided in order to be a part of this digital revolution,
sentences.zh: 大卫和他的商业伙伴，一个叫约翰·雷兹诺的人，决定为了参与这场数字革命，

sentences.en: they would found an internet company that hosted websites.
sentences.zh: 他们要创办一家托管网站的互联网公司。

sentences.en: The plan was straightforward enough.
sentences.zh: 计划非常简单直接。

sentences.en: David and John would provide the online space and some basic tools so that individuals or companies could build their own web page.
sentences.zh: 大卫和约翰提供在线空间和一些基本工具，以便个人或公司可以建立自己的网页。

sentences.en: And the company would host those pages on its servers.
sentences.zh: 公司则将这些页面托管在自己的服务器上。

sentences.en: And because their office was based in Beverly Hills, they named their company Beverly Hills Internet.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的办公室设在比佛利山庄，所以他们把公司命名为“比佛利山庄互联网”。

sentences.en: It will go down as having one of the worst names in history.
sentences.zh: 它将作为历史上最糟糕的名字之一被载入史册。

sentences.en: Actually, Beverly Hills Internet was doing okay at firSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，比佛利山庄互联网起初做得还不错。

sentences.en: It was starting to get some visitors to its website.
sentences.zh: 它的网站开始有一些访客了。

sentences.en: But John and David found it difficult to get the kind of sustainable traffic that they really wanted.
sentences.zh: 但约翰和大卫发现很难获得他们真正想要的持续流量。

sentences.en: Mostly because of one huge early 90s problem.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为90年代初的一个巨大难题。

sentences.en: What is internet anyway?
sentences.zh: 互联网到底是什么？

sentences.en: Internet is that massive computer network.
sentences.zh: 互联网就是那个庞大的计算机网络。

sentences.en: The one that's becoming really big now.
sentences.zh: 那个现在变得非常大的网络。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: How does one, what do you write to it like mail?
sentences.zh: 一个人怎么用它，你是像写信一样写给它吗？

sentences.en: Allison, can you explain what internet is?
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，你能解释一下什么是互联网吗？

sentences.en: A lot of people didn't really get what internet was.
sentences.zh: 很多人真的不明白互联网是什么。

sentences.en: Nobody really understood at the time what it meant to create a worldwide web of these kinds of connections where all computers were talking with one another and sharing information.
sentences.zh: 当时没人真正理解创造这种万维网连接意味着什么，即所有计算机都在相互交谈并共享信息。

sentences.en: So I had the challenge both trying to explain to my friends what I was trying to do and the wider world at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以我面临的挑战是，既要向朋友解释我在做什么，又要向更广阔的世界解释。

sentences.en: Even though today the internet is woven into our everyday lives,
sentences.zh: 尽管今天互联网已经融入了我们的日常生活，

sentences.en: it wasn't that long ago that people had to make this enormous leap from a world with essentially no internet to trying to conceptualize what a globally connected computer network meant or what they would even do with it.
sentences.zh: 但不久前，人们还必须从一个基本没有互联网的世界，跨越巨大的鸿沟，去尝试构想一个全球互联的计算机网络意味着什么，或者他们甚至能用它做什么。

sentences.en: Before search engines like Google or social networks or apps, the web seemed like this confusing, nebulous blob of information.
sentences.zh: 在谷歌等搜索引擎、社交网络或应用程序出现之前，网络看起来就像是一团令人困惑、模糊不清的信息块。

sentences.en: It was a strange new technology that was hard to wrap our brains around.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的新技术，很难让我们理解。

sentences.en: Because David ran an internet company, his business depended on users, having some grasp of what the internet was.
sentences.zh: 因为大卫经营着一家互联网公司，他的生意取决于用户对互联网的某种认知。

sentences.en: So it was his challenge to get people comfortable on the web.
sentences.zh: 所以他的挑战是让人们在网上感到舒适。

sentences.en: There's got, you know, we need to develop, we need to come up with something more.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们必须开发，我们必须想出更多东西。

sentences.en: He needed a hook.
sentences.zh: 他需要一个吸引点。

sentences.en: And one day in 1994, it just came to him.
sentences.zh: 1994年的一天，灵感突然降临。

sentences.en: His hosting site didn't need a technological innovation.
sentences.zh: 他的托管网站不需要技术创新。

sentences.en: It needed a conceptual one.
sentences.zh: 它需要的是概念上的创新。

sentences.en: Users needed a new way of navigating the web.
sentences.zh: 用户需要一种浏览网络的新方式。

sentences.en: So he sketched out a plan to make his website feel more like a real neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 于是他勾勒出一个计划，让他的网站感觉更像一个真实的社区。

sentences.en: You'd go through what was a two-dimensional representation of a neighborhood where you would see streets and blocks and you would see icons that represented houses.
sentences.zh: 你会穿过一个二维的社区表现形式，在那里你会看到街道和街区，还会看到代表房子的图标。

sentences.en: And you would actually pick an address that you wanted to create your website.
sentences.zh: 你实际上会选择一个地址来创建你的网站。

sentences.en: And you had a sense that you were joining a neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 你会有一种加入了一个社区的感觉。

sentences.en: David didn't want people to think of the web as something you logged on to, but more like a physical place to dwell in.
sentences.zh: 大卫不希望人们认为网络是一个你登录的地方，而更像是一个可以居住的物理场所。

sentences.en: Like a house.
sentences.zh: 就像房子一样。

sentences.en: When you signed up for a new webpage, that webpage was your house in an online community of your choosing.
sentences.zh: 当你注册一个新网页时，那个网页就是你在你选择的在线社区里的房子。

sentences.en: This was all a new frontier and you were in a way a virtual homesteader.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一个新的前沿领域，在某种程度上，你是一个虚拟的拓荒者。

sentences.en: David and his team were endowing users with a sense of digital manifest destiny, one virtual neighborhood at a time.
sentences.zh: 大卫和他的团队赋予了用户一种数字“天命昭昭”的感觉，一次一个虚拟社区。

sentences.en: It was such a revolutionary idea that David and his partner decided to chuck out the whole Beverly Hills internet name and change their company to something that fully leaned into the spatial metaphor they were creating.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此革命性的想法，以至于大卫和他的合伙人决定抛弃整个“比佛利山庄互联网”的名字，将公司改名为一个完全契合他们所创造的空间隐喻的名字。

sentences.en: They called it GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“地理城市”（GeoCities）。

sentences.en: The story of GeoCities is just a fantastic parallel for a real building, for something that was conceived of and created to model real life, but in the domain of cyberspace.
sentences.zh: GeoCities的故事是一个非常棒的真实建筑的平行案例，它是为了模拟现实生活而构思和创造的，但在网络空间领域。

sentences.en: And which ultimately had a catastrophic and dramatic fall in the end.
sentences.zh: 最终却以灾难性和戏剧性的方式走向了终结。

sentences.en: This is James Crawford, the author of Fallen Glory, The Lives and Deaths of History's Greatest Buildings.
sentences.zh: 这是詹姆斯·克劳福德，《陨落的荣耀：历史上最伟大建筑的生与死》的作者。

sentences.en: GeoCities was not a physical place.
sentences.zh: GeoCities不是一个物理场所。

sentences.en: But he included it in his book because the way he sees it, it was inhabited like one.
sentences.zh: 但他把它写进了书里，因为在他看来，它就像一个地方一样被居住着。

sentences.en: And that was something that I think GeoCities was really providing, was creating these communities and then conceptualizing them as places.
sentences.zh: 我认为GeoCities真正提供的是创造这些社区，然后将它们概念化为地方。

sentences.en: As places you could go, as neighborhoods on the net.
sentences.zh: 作为你可以去的地方，作为网络上的社区。

sentences.en: So you could be a citizen of a city, of a country, and you could then be a netizen of somewhere like GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以是一个城市、一个国家的公民，然后你也可以成为像GeoCities这样的地方的网民。

sentences.en: The website was a collection of metropolises, each with their own neighborhoods built around shared interests.
sentences.zh: 该网站是一个大都市的集合，每个大都市都有围绕共同兴趣建立的社区。

sentences.en: There was a region called Heartland, where you could discuss tractor models.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫“心脏地带”的区域，你可以在那里讨论拖拉机型号。

sentences.en: Or Petsburg, where you could talk endlessly about your cats.
sentences.zh: 或者“宠物堡”，你可以在那里无休止地谈论你的猫。

sentences.en: Or in Area 51, you could find page after page after page of fan tributes to Dana Scully.
sentences.zh: 或者在“51区”，你可以找到一页又一页关于丹娜·斯卡利的粉丝致敬页面。

sentences.en: As soon as David established this spatialized version of the web, GeoCities really began to click for people.
sentences.zh: 大卫一建立这种空间化的网络版本，GeoCities就真正开始受到人们的欢迎了。

sentences.en: David remembers how in the early days, he set up a little alert to go off anytime someone registered for a new account.
sentences.zh: 大卫记得在早期，他设置了一个小提醒，每当有人注册新账户时就会响起。

sentences.en: So I'd be sitting in my office and we'd go, dang.
sentences.zh: 所以我坐在办公室里，我们会听到“叮”。

sentences.en: And someone would say, what's that?
sentences.zh: 有人会问，那是什么？

sentences.en: And I would say, well, somebody just registered for their own page at GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 我会说，哦，有人刚刚注册了他们在GeoCities的个人主页。

sentences.en: And they said, oh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，那很酷。

sentences.en: Then it would go, dang.
sentences.zh: 然后它又会响，“叮”。

sentences.en: And then it really started to take off.
sentences.zh: 然后它真的开始腾飞了。

sentences.en: Ultimately, it was just nonstop.
sentences.zh: 最终，它简直是没完没了。

sentences.en: Ding, ding, ding, ding, ding.
sentences.zh: 叮，叮，叮，叮，叮。

sentences.en: I mean, it was just, it was really, really exciting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的、真的非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: You know, I would start to hear like, I mean, this is happening a lot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会开始听到，我的意思是，这发生得太频繁了。

sentences.en: And so I had, of course, I had, I turned it off because it was too disruptive.
sentences.zh: 所以当然，我把它关掉了，因为它太吵了。

sentences.en: David wanted users who built their webpages in GeoCities to feel like part of a community.
sentences.zh: 大卫希望在GeoCities建立网页的用户能感觉自己是社区的一部分。

sentences.en: That no matter how obscure their interests were, they could find a neighbor who felt just as passionately as they did about Star Trek or 12th century Norse mythology.
sentences.zh: 无论他们的兴趣多么冷门，他们都能找到一个和他们一样对《星际迷航》或12世纪北欧神话充满热情的邻居。

sentences.en: I think a lot of that comes from my own experiences as a gay man and coming out and meeting other lesbian and gay people
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上源于我作为一名男同性恋者的个人经历，出柜并结识其他女同性恋和男同性恋者，

sentences.en: and understanding the power of meeting others of your own identity.
sentences.zh: 并理解结识与你有相同身份的人的力量。

sentences.en: I think people came to it with more open minds and less desire to be performative in how they were interacting online.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们带着更开放的心态来到这里，减少了在网上互动时的表演欲。

sentences.en: It was this fleeting moment when users seem more interested in making human connections and honest self-expression than in cultivating a web persona.
sentences.zh: 那是一个短暂的时刻，用户似乎对建立人际联系和诚实的自我表达比培养网络人设更感兴趣。

sentences.en: They just wanted to build something.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想建造点什么。

sentences.en: They wanted to build something.
sentences.zh: 他们想建造点什么。

sentences.en: Dedicated to Dana Scully.
sentences.zh: 献给丹娜·斯卡利。

sentences.en: I was looking to give everybody the tools to create their own content and celebrate the terrific diversity and richness and tapestry of content created by users.
sentences.zh: 我当时想给每个人提供工具来创作他们自己的内容，并赞美用户创造的内容所具有的惊人多样性、丰富性和挂毯般的质感。

sentences.en: There were, of course, some limitations to user-generated content.
sentences.zh: 当然，用户生成的内容也有一些局限性。

sentences.en: GeoCities was a website that was built by amateurs.
sentences.zh: GeoCities是一个由业余爱好者建立的网站。

sentences.en: And it showed.
sentences.zh: 而且显而易见。

sentences.en: The color palettes of most GeoCities pages seemed like they were chosen randomly.
sentences.zh: 大多数GeoCities页面的配色方案看起来像是随机选择的。

sentences.en: Or maybe even chosen with the intention of making them illegible.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是为了让人看不清而选择的。

sentences.en: Like neon green texts over a neon yellow background.
sentences.zh: 比如霓虹黄背景上的霓虹绿文字。

sentences.en: There were under construction signs, twinkling star backgrounds, grainy low-res family photos, welcome to my homepage GIFs.
sentences.zh: 到处都是“施工中”标志、闪烁的星星背景、颗粒感十足的低分辨率家庭照片、“欢迎来到我的主页”GIF图。

sentences.en: Or GIFs of dancing babies.
sentences.zh: 或者是跳舞婴儿的GIF图。

sentences.en: You know, it was the Wild WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是蛮荒西部。

sentences.en: Just different styles and different page layouts and different menus bars and even, you know, experimenting with menus and pages that were only menus.
sentences.zh: 只是不同的风格、不同的页面布局、不同的菜单栏，甚至，你知道，尝试使用菜单和只有菜单的页面。

sentences.en: There was an absolute obsession with comic songs, font.
sentences.zh: 当时对Comic Sans字体有一种绝对的痴迷。

sentences.en: You know, all these kind of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Flashing GIFs.
sentences.zh: 闪烁的GIF图。

sentences.en: All these things that are almost feel like a kind of early vomitus of the internet.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西几乎感觉像是互联网早期的呕吐物。

sentences.en: Looking back through the lens of the flat design and minimalism that came after, it's hard to click through these pages without having a chuckle.
sentences.zh: 透过后来扁平化设计和极简主义的镜头回顾，很难在浏览这些页面时不发出笑声。

sentences.en: It was a whole lot messier and much more chaotic.
sentences.zh: 它要混乱得多，也杂乱得多。

sentences.en: But the pages built on GeoCities reflected this amazing moment when people were attempting to figure out what the internet was and what it could be.
sentences.zh: 但GeoCities上建立的页面反映了那个惊人的时刻，当时人们正试图弄清楚互联网是什么，以及它能成为什么。

sentences.en: It's this beginning of the creation of web culture.
sentences.zh: 这是网络文化创造的开端。

sentences.en: And that's what's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 而这正是最有趣的地方。

sentences.en: It's the beginning of personal website.
sentences.zh: 这是个人网站的开端。

sentences.en: It's translating your life, who you are, and putting it online.
sentences.zh: 这是在翻译你的生活，你是谁，并把它放到网上。

sentences.en: By 1998, GeoCities was the third most visited website on the internet, just after Yahoo.
sentences.zh: 到1998年，GeoCities是互联网上访问量第三大的网站，仅次于雅虎。

sentences.en: In fact, Yahoo was so impressed with GeoCities' rapid ascent that they bought the company from David.
sentences.zh: 事实上，雅虎对GeoCities的迅速崛起印象深刻，以至于他们从大卫手中买下了这家公司。

sentences.en: Executives at GeoCities believed that combining forces with Yahoo would put the website on steroids.
sentences.zh: GeoCities的高管们认为，与雅虎联手会让网站如虎添翼。

sentences.en: But that wasn't what most GeoCities users wanted.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是大多数GeoCities用户想要的。

sentences.en: Users had legitimate concerns that, you know, GeoCities will lose its independence and its identity, which is ultimately what happened.
sentences.zh: 用户有合理的担忧，你知道，GeoCities会失去它的独立性和身份，而这最终确实发生了。

sentences.en: After the purchase, GeoCities users woke up to a notice saying they had to re-register, granting Yahoo the rights to
sentences.zh: 收购后，GeoCities用户醒来时看到一条通知，说他们必须重新注册，授予雅虎权利，

sentences.en: Meaning all of the content on the website would now be owned by Yahoo.
sentences.zh: 这意味着网站上的所有内容现在都归雅虎所有。

sentences.en: Many threatened to leave the city in proteSt.
sentences.zh: 许多人威胁要离开这个城市以示抗议。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, Yahoo actually agreed to alter their terms of service.
sentences.zh: 结果，雅虎确实同意修改了他们的服务条款。

sentences.en: It was, though, the first real sign of unrest in the city.
sentences.zh: 不过，这是城市中第一次出现真正的不安迹象。

sentences.en: If you like, it was the moment that signaled just the very beginning of the end.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，这就是标志着终结之始的时刻。

sentences.en: It was the beginning of the end not just for GeoCities, but for a ton of internet companies around the web.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是GeoCities的终结之始，也是网络上大量互联网公司的终结之始。

sentences.en: The dot-com bubble had been rapidly inflating throughout the late 90s because investors were pouring money into internet startups left and right and just crossing their fingers that one day they'd be profitable.
sentences.zh: 互联网泡沫在整个90年代末迅速膨胀，因为投资者不断向互联网初创公司投入资金，并祈祷有一天它们能盈利。

sentences.en: There was actually a mantra that you weren't a successful dot-com company unless you were losing money.
sentences.zh: 当时甚至有一种口号，说如果你不亏钱，你就不是一家成功的互联网公司。

sentences.en: By the year 2001, the bubble had burst and corporations like Yahoo were losing their footing.
sentences.zh: 到了2001年，泡沫破裂，像雅虎这样的公司开始站不稳脚跟了。

sentences.en: The internet was starting to change faSt.
sentences.zh: 互联网开始飞速改变。

sentences.en: Up until this point, a lot of users had been working in a static, entry-level version of the internet.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，许多用户一直是在一个静态的、入门级的互联网版本中活动。

sentences.en: It was more homemade, identifiable by those vibrant personal pages hand-built by users.
sentences.zh: 它更像是家庭作坊式的，其标志就是用户亲手搭建的那些充满活力的个人主页。

sentences.en: It's where GeoCities had thrived.
sentences.zh: 那是 GeoCities 曾经繁荣的地方。

sentences.en: But by the time the new millennium rolled around, the internet was evolving into a whole new experience.
sentences.zh: 但当新千年到来时，互联网正在演变成一种全新的体验。

sentences.en: This internet was based around interactive social networking sites.
sentences.zh: 这种互联网基于交互式的社交网站。

sentences.en: You would punch in your name, age, and relationship status, and the site would spit out a manicured profile page.
sentences.zh: 你输入姓名、年龄和感情状态，网站就会吐出一个精心修饰的个人资料页。

sentences.en: Users were encouraged to write on each other's walls and tag and comment.
sentences.zh: 用户被鼓励在彼此的留言板上留言、打标签和评论。

sentences.en: GeoCities had created this great spatial metaphor to help people understand the web, but users were outgrowing that metaphor.
sentences.zh: GeoCities 创造了一个伟大的空间隐喻来帮助人们理解网络，但用户已经不再满足于那个隐喻了。

sentences.en: Having a GeoCities page began to feel embarrassing to a lot of users, which is basically a death sentence for any platform.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个 GeoCities 页面开始让许多用户感到尴尬，这对任何平台来说基本上都是死刑判决。

sentences.en: I'm going to check out my GeoCities account.
sentences.zh: 我要去看看我的 GeoCities 账户。

sentences.en: Hold on!
sentences.zh: 等等！

sentences.en: Let me crank up the computer!
sentences.zh: 让我启动电脑！

sentences.en: The computer!
sentences.zh: 电脑！

sentences.en: I suppose because we're so close to it, and we know the people who created these.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为我们离它太近了，而且我们认识那些创造这些东西的人。

sentences.en: You know, maybe they're our parents, maybe they're our older brothers or sisters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他们是我们的父母，也许是我们的哥哥姐姐。

sentences.en: And we don't necessarily respect it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们未必会尊重它。

sentences.en: Yahoo's stock started to plummet shortly after it bought GeoCities, and year after year the site was losing more users.
sentences.zh: 雅虎在收购 GeoCities 后不久，股价就开始暴跌，而且该网站的用户逐年流失。

sentences.en: From a business perspective, GeoCities seemed like dead weight.
sentences.zh: 从商业角度来看，GeoCities 似乎成了累赘。

sentences.en: July 2009, they send what they call a service announcement.
sentences.zh: 2009 年 7 月，他们发布了所谓的“服务公告”。

sentences.en: And all it says is that GeoCities is closing, and all files are going to be deleted from servers and will not be recoverable.
sentences.zh: 公告里只说 GeoCities 即将关闭，所有文件都将从服务器上删除，且无法恢复。

sentences.en: GeoCities was about to be completely wiped out, as if it had never existed.
sentences.zh: GeoCities 即将被彻底抹去，仿佛它从未存在过一样。

sentences.en: You know, even if you look at something like the dropping of a nuclear bomb, that still leaves ruins, it still leaves people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使你看像投下原子弹这样的事情，它仍然会留下废墟，仍然会留下人。

sentences.en: You know, those people can then grow something from the ashes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些人随后可以从灰烬中重建一些东西。

sentences.en: This is an absolute existential deletion of existence.
sentences.zh: 而这是一种绝对的、存在意义上的彻底删除。

sentences.en: You know, it is just taken, and it is gone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它就这样被拿走，然后消失了。

sentences.en: This was the wholesale destruction of a website that changed the way that people looked at the internet.
sentences.zh: 这是对一个改变了人们看待互联网方式的网站的全面摧毁。

sentences.en: A lot of people believed that these pages deserved to be saved.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为这些页面值得被保存下来。

sentences.en: And a handful of people decided to actually do something about it.
sentences.zh: 于是少数人决定真正采取行动。

sentences.en: But there's this sense always that, like, the web is permanent.
sentences.zh: 但人们总有一种感觉，觉得网络是永久的。

sentences.en: Like, if you do something terrible, it's on the internet forever.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你做了什么可怕的事，它会永远留在互联网上。

sentences.en: And if you have one embarrassing photo and someone shares it, it'll never go away.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一张尴尬的照片被别人分享了，它就永远不会消失。

sentences.en: And I'm here to tell you that, no, it'll probably all go away.
sentences.zh: 但我在这里要告诉你，不，它很可能会全部消失。

sentences.en: This is Jason Scott.
sentences.zh: 这位是 Jason Scott。

sentences.en: Jason actually has a few roles.
sentences.zh: Jason 其实身兼数职。

sentences.en: He's a digital archivist, historian, software curator, angel of death.
sentences.zh: 他是数字档案管理员、历史学家、软件策展人，也是“死亡天使”。

sentences.en: So the reason I'm known as the angel of death is because I have successfully let people know that when a certain kind of situation happens, call Jason Scott.
sentences.zh: 我之所以被称为“死亡天使”，是因为我已经成功让人们知道，当某种情况发生时，就打给 Jason Scott。

sentences.en: The situation is that a website is on the brink of its demise, and all of its digital information is about to be lost forever.
sentences.zh: 这种情况就是：一个网站正处于灭亡边缘，其所有的数字信息都即将永远丢失。

sentences.en: Jason's job is to swoop in and download all of that data before it's gone for good.
sentences.zh: Jason 的工作就是在网站彻底消失前，迅速介入并下载所有数据。

sentences.en: And, like the angel of death, Jason's face is the last thing that a dying website sees before it's gone for good.
sentences.zh: 而且，就像死亡天使一样，Jason 的脸是垂死的网站在彻底消失前看到的最后一样东西。

sentences.en: Back in 2009, before he became the go-to savior of the old web, Jason was noticing more and more that old-school hosting services like GeoCities were going dark.
sentences.zh: 早在 2009 年，在他成为旧网络的首选救星之前，Jason 就越来越频繁地注意到像 GeoCities 这样的老牌托管服务正在走向没落。

sentences.en: He couldn't stop thinking about all the user-generated content that was being destroyed in the process.
sentences.zh: 他无法停止思考在这个过程中被摧毁的所有用户生成内容。

sentences.en: The one that still haunts me is this woman who, in 1994, made an entire website in HTML about her child who had died when he was two.
sentences.zh: 至今仍让我无法释怀的是一位女士，她在 1994 年用 HTML 制作了一个完整的网站，纪念她两岁时去世的孩子。

sentences.en: And she's got a little, you know, candle gif and a little MIDI song playing in the background.
sentences.zh: 她放了一个小小的蜡烛 GIF 动图，背景里还播放着一首小小的 MIDI 音乐。

sentences.en: And this was her story.
sentences.zh: 这就是她的故事。

sentences.en: Jason wanted to make sure sites like GeoCities and their data weren't just erased.
sentences.zh: Jason 想确保像 GeoCities 这样的网站及其数据不会就这样被抹去。

sentences.en: So we connected with a group of like-minded digital preservation enthusiasts scattered around the world.
sentences.zh: 于是我们联系了一群散布在世界各地、志同道合的数字保存爱好者。

sentences.en: And they drafted a plan.
sentences.zh: 他们起草了一份计划。

sentences.en: Somebody should come in.
sentences.zh: 应该有人介入。

sentences.en: There should be an A-team, an archive team, that rushes in and makes a copy.
sentences.zh: 应该有一个“A 队”，一个档案团队，冲进去并进行备份。

sentences.en: Wouldn't that be something?
sentences.zh: 那岂不是很棒？

sentences.en: So we announced that we're Archive Team.
sentences.zh: 于是我们宣布成立“档案团队”（Archive Team）。

sentences.en: We're going to rescue your s**t.
sentences.zh: 我们要拯救你们的烂摊子。

sentences.en: And that was our slogan.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的口号。

sentences.en: We're going to rescue your s**t.
sentences.zh: 我们要拯救你们的烂摊子。

sentences.en: Archive Team decided their mission was to keep an eye out for websites in danger of being shut down.
sentences.zh: 档案团队决定他们的使命是留意那些面临关闭危险的网站。

sentences.en: The ones that they say are on Death Watch.
sentences.zh: 那些他们称之为处于“死亡观察”名单上的网站。

sentences.en: And download every piece of data they could before that site goes dark.
sentences.zh: 并在网站下线前下载他们能获取的每一份数据。

sentences.en: Their goal is to preserve digital heritage no matter how small.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是保存数字遗产，无论其规模有多小。

sentences.en: And their first project, GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 而他们的第一个项目就是 GeoCities。

sentences.en: For us, it was worth it because we hate Yahoo.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，这是值得的，因为我们讨厌雅虎。

sentences.en: But it wasn't solely about saying up yours to Yahoo.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是为了对雅虎说“去你的”。

sentences.en: Okay, well, that was a very big part of it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那确实是其中很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: But it was also about something bigger.
sentences.zh: 但它也关乎更宏大的意义。

sentences.en: I also wanted people to kind of get knocked in the head about the impermanence of digital information.
sentences.zh: 我还想让人们意识到数字信息的非永久性，给他们当头一棒。

sentences.en: That it was both brittle and easily lost, but also with a little bit of care, easily saved and kept.
sentences.zh: 它既脆弱且容易丢失，但只要稍微用点心，也很容易被保存和留存。

sentences.en: Archive Team had a dual mission.
sentences.zh: 档案团队有着双重使命。

sentences.en: In addition to preserving things, they also want us to understand that digital information is fragile.
sentences.zh: 除了保存事物，他们还想让我们明白数字信息是脆弱的。

sentences.en: The profiles you build on any social media site, the videos you upload to YouTube, they all exist out of your hands and on some corporation servers.
sentences.zh: 你在任何社交媒体网站上建立的个人资料、你上传到 YouTube 的视频，它们都不在你的掌控之中，而是存在于某些公司的服务器上。

sentences.en: And they can vanish at any given moment.
sentences.zh: 它们随时可能消失。

sentences.en: They have no idea that it can literally, literally disappear in a week or a day.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道它真的、真的可能在一天或一周内就消失不见。

sentences.en: And it just come to it and there's an error and it's gone.
sentences.zh: 你访问它时，只会看到一个错误提示，然后它就没了。

sentences.en: And I get to see that over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 而我一次又一次地目睹这种情况发生。

sentences.en: So that's, you know, I'm delighted that they're making these worlds and I'm cynical about how long they laSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我很高兴他们创造了这些世界，但我对它们能持续多久持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Yahoo had hinted in early 2009 that it would be closing down the service sometime later that year.
sentences.zh: 雅虎在 2009 年初曾暗示将在那年晚些时候关闭该服务。

sentences.en: So GeoCities could have maybe a few months or a few days.
sentences.zh: 所以 GeoCities 可能只剩下几个月甚至几天的时间了。

sentences.en: Archive Team got to work immediately trying to recruit as many people as possible
sentences.zh: 档案团队立即开始工作，试图招募尽可能多的人

sentences.en: to help with what Jason referred to as GeoCities download-a-palooza.
sentences.zh: 来帮助 Jason 所说的“GeoCities 下载狂欢”。

sentences.en: I started using whatever social media capital I had at the time.
sentences.zh: 我开始利用我当时拥有的所有社交媒体资本。

sentences.en: And about 200, I think 300 people in total came in and it was really lumpy.
sentences.zh: 我想总共有大约 200 到 300 人参与进来，过程非常零散。

sentences.en: They had their computers crawling Yahoo servers to pull out any piece of public GeoCities data they could get.
sentences.zh: 他们让电脑爬取雅虎服务器，尽可能地提取出每一份公开的 GeoCities 数据。

sentences.en: And we were just doing it day in and day out and saying, OK, who wants to take this part over?
sentences.zh: 我们没日没夜地干，问着：“好，谁想接手这一部分？”

sentences.en: Who wants to do this part?
sentences.zh: “谁想做那一部分？”

sentences.en: Let's look for this.
sentences.zh: “让我们找找这个。”

sentences.en: Let's do searches on the web for every noun in the dictionary.
sentences.zh: “让我们在网上搜索字典里的每一个名词。”

sentences.en: Try to find every GeoCities site that mentions any noun and then try to compile them into a unique set
sentences.zh: 试着找出每一个提到任何名词的 GeoCities 网站，然后试着把它们汇编成一个独特的数据集，

sentences.en: and then assign it to people to download.
sentences.zh: 然后分配给人们去下载。

sentences.en: Then, on October 26, 2009, after six months of work, the day they all dreaded finally came.
sentences.zh: 接着，在 2009 年 10 月 26 日，经过六个月的工作，他们最担心的那一天终于来了。

sentences.en: Archive Team watched from their respective computers as the digital city slowly went offline for good.
sentences.zh: 档案团队在各自的电脑前注视着这座数字城市慢慢地永远下线。

sentences.en: Jason said that watching Yahoo pull the plug was like something out of 2001 A Space Odyssey.
sentences.zh: Jason 说，看着雅虎拔掉电源就像《2001 太空漫游》里的情节。

sentences.en: It is exactly like shutting down HAL.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像关闭 HAL（人工智能电脑）。

sentences.en: And we will be like, this set has gone down.
sentences.zh: 我们会说：“这个数据集已经下线了。”

sentences.en: They've now powered down this server.
sentences.zh: “他们现在关闭了这个服务器。”

sentences.en: They've now powered down this server.
sentences.zh: “他们现在关闭了这个服务器。”

sentences.en: Archive Team was still working as fast as possible to grab whatever GeoCities data was left,
sentences.zh: 档案团队仍在尽可能快地工作，以抓取剩下的任何 GeoCities 数据，

sentences.en: while the servers went dark one by one.
sentences.zh: 同时服务器一个接一个地变黑。

sentences.en: And we're like, here it goes.
sentences.zh: 我们说：“开始了。”

sentences.en: We just lost this one.
sentences.zh: “我们刚刚丢掉了这个。”

sentences.en: We just lost this one.
sentences.zh: “我们刚刚丢掉了这个。”

sentences.en: Keep going.
sentences.zh: “继续。”

sentences.en: Keep going.
sentences.zh: “继续。”

sentences.en: And we're just going until finally it's just not responding meaningfully at all.
sentences.zh: 我们一直持续到最后它完全没有任何有意义的响应。

sentences.en: I mean, that's pretty much the ending of every one of these stories is us packing up the boxes, putting them on the pallets, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些故事的结局几乎都是我们打包箱子，把它们装上托盘，你知道的。

sentences.en: So it's this pride that we got the job done, but it really feels like we lifted a piano up 20 stories and then took it down again, you know, 20 minutes later.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种完成了任务的自豪感，但感觉真的就像我们把一架钢琴抬上 20 楼，然后 20 分钟后又把它搬下来一样，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Like, yep, we were good piano movers.
sentences.zh: 就像是：“没错，我们是优秀的钢琴搬运工。”

sentences.en: But it wasn't all for nothing.
sentences.zh: 但这一切并非毫无意义。

sentences.en: In the end, Archive Team managed to extract a terabyte of data from GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 最终，档案团队成功从 GeoCities 提取了 1TB 的数据。

sentences.en: And as it turns out, there were multiple parallel projects that were downloading GeoCities data.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，还有多个并行项目也在下载 GeoCities 数据。

sentences.en: A lot of them have sent their data to Jason for safekeeping.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人把数据发给了 Jason 以便妥善保存。

sentences.en: Altogether, Archive Team saved more than a million accounts from deletion.
sentences.zh: 总共，档案团队从删除中拯救了超过一百万个账户。

sentences.en: Archive Team wanted to bring some attention to their work.
sentences.zh: 档案团队想让人们关注他们的工作。

sentences.en: So they took all of that GeoCities data they'd preserved and they turned it into a torrent on the Pirate Bay.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把所有保存下来的 GeoCities 数据做成了一个种子文件，发布在海盗湾（Pirate Bay）上。

sentences.en: The Pirate Bay is generally used for illegally downloading games, movies and software.
sentences.zh: 海盗湾通常用于非法下载游戏、电影和软件。

sentences.en: So no one really saw this coming.
sentences.zh: 所以没人预料到会这样。

sentences.en: We were like, we have the hottest new wear for you.
sentences.zh: 我们说：“我们有最热门的新资源给你们。”

sentences.en: Here's GeoCities.
sentences.zh: “这是 GeoCities。”

sentences.en: And it was the largest torrent at its time.
sentences.zh: 它是当时最大的种子文件。

sentences.en: It broke everything.
sentences.zh: 它搞崩了一切。

sentences.en: And when it got uncompressed, it turned out Windows machines couldn't handle it.
sentences.zh: 当它被解压时，Windows 机器根本处理不了。

sentences.en: People were furious because it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 人们非常愤怒，因为这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Like, why am I doing this?
sentences.zh: 就像：“我为什么要这么做？”

sentences.en: It's telling me I have, you know, 19 months to download.
sentences.zh: “它告诉我需要 19 个月才能下载完。”

sentences.en: Surely it's some sort of top secret, you know, allocation of information of the darkest parts of the web.
sentences.zh: 人们肯定以为这是某种绝密信息，是网络最黑暗部分的资源分配。

sentences.en: And it's like, no, it's cats and it's lots of rock and roll fan sites and it's families telling you that they're going to have a barbecue.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，不，里面全是猫咪图片、摇滚乐迷网站，还有家庭告诉大家他们要举办烧烤聚会的信息。

sentences.en: Jason wasn't sure what people would actually do with the GeoCities data, but that really wasn't his concern.
sentences.zh: Jason 不确定人们会用这些 GeoCities 数据做什么，但这并不是他关心的重点。

sentences.en: He just wanted to make sure that it was safe and available to anyone who wanted it.
sentences.zh: 他只是想确保数据是安全的，并且对任何想要它的人开放。

sentences.en: And maybe if he was lucky, something useful would come out of it down the line.
sentences.zh: 如果幸运的话，也许未来能从中挖掘出有用的东西。

sentences.en: I long ago got out of the argument of what good is this.
sentences.zh: 我早就放弃了争论“这有什么用”的问题。

sentences.en: Actually, a number of people have downloaded the GeoCities torrent and have made some really cool projects with that data.
sentences.zh: 事实上，已经有很多人下载了 GeoCities 种子，并利用这些数据制作了一些非常酷的项目。

sentences.en: A good amount of GeoCities pages have been restored and you can browse through them online.
sentences.zh: 相当一部分 GeoCities 页面已经被恢复，你可以在线浏览它们。

sentences.en: Since saving GeoCities, Jason and the archive team have preserved a number of dying websites around the internet.
sentences.zh: 自拯救 GeoCities 以来，Jason 和档案团队已经保存了互联网上许多濒临消失的网站。

sentences.en: From Yahoo Groups to Justin.tv.
sentences.zh: 从雅虎群组（Yahoo Groups）到 Justin.tv。

sentences.en: It's all accessible on a digital archive called Wayback Machine, where you can find over 477 billion saved web pages.
sentences.zh: 这一切都可以在一个名为“互联网档案馆”（Wayback Machine）的数字档案库中访问，在那里你可以找到超过 4770 亿个保存的网页。

sentences.en: The Wayback Machine was founded by the Internet Archive, where Jason Scott is now an archiviSt.
sentences.zh: Wayback Machine 由互联网档案馆（Internet Archive）创立，Jason Scott 现在就是那里的档案管理员。

sentences.en: A lot of time and energy went into rescuing GeoCities, along with a ton of other archaic sites from this generation of the web.
sentences.zh: 拯救 GeoCities 以及这一代网络中大量其他古老网站投入了大量的时间和精力。

sentences.en: But I want to be clear.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说明一点。

sentences.en: None of this was salvaged as examples of how well the web worked back in the day.
sentences.zh: 这些东西被抢救下来，并不是为了展示当年的网络有多么好用。

sentences.en: No one needs more Netscape Now buttons or Backstreet Boys fan pages.
sentences.zh: 没人需要更多的“Netscape Now”按钮或后街男孩（Backstreet Boys）的粉丝页面。

sentences.en: I think we're good on Backstreet Boys fan pages.
sentences.zh: 我想后街男孩的粉丝页面已经够多了。

sentences.en: The point is, these archives should be studied.
sentences.zh: 重点是，这些档案应该被研究。

sentences.en: Because our web history is our history.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的网络历史就是我们的历史。

sentences.en: No matter how goofy it might appear.
sentences.zh: 无论它看起来多么滑稽。

sentences.en: If the Internet's history were sketched to look like the March of Progress, that famous illustration charting human evolution with an ape on one side and a man on the other,
sentences.zh: 如果互联网的历史被画成“人类进步图”，那幅著名的展示人类进化的插图，一边是猿猴，另一边是人类，

sentences.en: GeoCities would be like that third guy from the right, a little hairy, a little clumsy, but definitely an important link that made us what we are today.
sentences.zh: GeoCities 就像是从右边数第三个家伙，有点毛茸茸的，有点笨拙，但绝对是让我们成为今天这个样子的重要一环。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not necessarily art, but it's absolutely culture.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它未必是艺术，但绝对是文化。

sentences.en: James Crawford again.
sentences.zh: 再次提到 James Crawford。

sentences.en: You know, this is what we've always done as humans, you know, going back to the earliest marks we put on the caves, is you're presented with a surface.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是我们人类一直以来所做的，追溯到我们在洞穴上留下的最早标记，当你面对一个表面时，

sentences.en: And what do you do with it?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: How do you mark it?
sentences.zh: 你如何标记它？

sentences.en: How do you represent who you are on that space?
sentences.zh: 你如何在那片空间里展现你是谁？

sentences.en: And, you know, a number of people have made this comparison between the kind of cave paintings of Lascaux and what was happening in GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人把拉斯科洞窟壁画和GeoCities上发生的事情做了类比。

sentences.en: And it seems like a bizarre, almost absurd comparison to make.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是一个离奇，甚至荒谬的类比。

sentences.en: But actually, if we fast forward another 10,000 years and look back, that's absolutely what it was.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果我们把时间快进一万年再回过头来看，这绝对就是那么回事。

sentences.en: It was people grappling with a new technology and how to represent their humanity in that space.
sentences.zh: 那是人们在努力应对一种新技术，并试图在那个空间里展现他们的人性。

sentences.en: You can imagine thousands of years from now, past the boundary of the cringy recent past, to a future human, dusting off an old PC desktop from 1997, finding a GeoCities torrent,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下，几千年后，跨越了近期那些令人尴尬的过去，未来的某个人掸去一台1997年旧电脑上的灰尘，找到了一个GeoCities的种子文件，

sentences.en: and taking an anthropological exploration of what's inside.
sentences.zh: 并对里面的内容进行了一次人类学探索。

sentences.en: So, the first thing they're going to do is just waste a week trying to figure out if they're getting the colors wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们要做的第一件事就是浪费一周时间，试图弄清楚是不是自己把颜色搞错了。

sentences.en: Like, they're going to look at these backgrounds and they're going to be like, this is objectively illegible.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们看着这些背景，会觉得这简直是客观上的无法辨认。

sentences.en: And they're going to check the specs, check the specs and go, nope, those people had no taste.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会去查规格，查完规格后说，不，那些人真是毫无品味。

sentences.en: What was going on there?
sentences.zh: 那时到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And the answer was, the sky was the limit.
sentences.zh: 答案是，一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: So, why not yellow on pink?
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么不能用粉色底黄色字呢？

sentences.en: Why not blinking text saying that this is your homepage and then an animated GIF with three frames of a waving care bear right next to your description of, you know,
sentences.zh: 为什么不能在你的主页介绍旁边，放上一段写着“这是我的主页”的闪烁文字，再配上一个三帧挥手的爱心熊动态GIF，顺便写上，你知道，

sentences.en: love for Jesus?
sentences.zh: 对耶稣的爱？

sentences.en: This future person is going to discover a tiny window of web history where people were trying their best to chart a course through completely unknown territory.
sentences.zh: 这位未来的人将发现网络历史上的一小段窗口期，那时的人们正竭尽全力在完全未知的领域中摸索前行。

sentences.en: Where users took chances and weren't ashamed to look a little messy or garish or hopeful.
sentences.zh: 那里的用户敢于冒险，不羞于表现得凌乱、花哨或充满希望。

sentences.en: They're going to see this boundless joy of people who are unfettered by feeling that they have to sell themselves to present their best faces.
sentences.zh: 他们会看到人们那种无拘无束的快乐，不受那种必须推销自己、展示最好一面的感觉所束缚。

sentences.en: And they'll see a lot of lies, a lot of truth, a lot of honesty.
sentences.zh: 他们会看到很多谎言，很多真相，很多真诚。

sentences.en: But it's going to come from a person talking to you.
sentences.zh: 但这都将来自一个正在与你对话的人。

sentences.en: Because GeoCities made it easy to work in the code of the web, but it didn't teach you to be a performer.
sentences.zh: 因为GeoCities让人很容易上手网页代码，但它并没有教你如何成为一个表演者。

sentences.en: So, that's what they're going to find.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是他们会发现的东西。

sentences.en: And they're not going to believe it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们会难以置信。

sentences.en: They're going to assume this was all a trick.
sentences.zh: 他们会认为这一切都是某种把戏。

sentences.en: Nobody could be this nice.
sentences.zh: 没人能这么友善。

sentences.en: Nobody could be this forward.
sentences.zh: 没人能这么直率。

sentences.en: No one could be this personal.
sentences.zh: 没人能这么私人化。

sentences.en: But they were.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: We have another story about a different virtual apocalypse after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们还有另一个关于不同虚拟世界末日的故事。

sentences.en: So, we're back with Vivian, who brought us that story about GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 我们回来了，Vivian带给我们那个关于GeoCities的故事。

sentences.en: Hey, Viv.
sentences.zh: 嘿，Viv。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: So, one of the reasons why we do these codes is we have all this stuff that's on the cutting room floor that doesn't quite fit into the story.
sentences.zh: 我们做这些节目的原因之一，是因为我们有很多被剪掉的素材，它们不太适合放进正片里。

sentences.en: But it's so good that we just want to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 但它们又太棒了，我们忍不住想聊聊。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们来聊聊吧。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: something that we kind of alluded to in the main piece but didn't really spend a lot of time getting into was the afterlife of the GeoCities data that was saved by Archive Team.
sentences.zh: 我们在正片中提到过，但没有花太多时间深入探讨的一点，是Archive Team保存的GeoCities数据的后续。

sentences.en: So, we kind of focused on like the life, death, and preservations of GeoCities.
sentences.zh: 我们主要关注的是GeoCities的生、死和保存过程。

sentences.en: But we didn't really dip into what people have done with it afterwards because the story kind of felt complete on its own.
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有深入探讨人们后来用它做了什么，因为那个故事本身已经很完整了。

sentences.en: But there's a lot there.
sentences.zh: 但那里面的内容非常丰富。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: So, what are people making with this GeoCities data?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们用这些GeoCities数据制作了什么？

sentences.en: Probably one of my favorite projects is this website called Cameron'sWorld.net, which was created by this web designer named Cameron Askin.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的项目之一是一个叫Cameron'sWorld.net的网站，它是由一位名叫Cameron Askin的网页设计师创建的。

sentences.en: And I don't really know how to describe it other than saying it's like everything that the Space Jam website wishes it was.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么形容它，只能说它就像是《空中大灌篮》网站所希望成为的一切。

sentences.en: Like, I really don't know how to explain it.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道该怎么解释。

sentences.en: But it's just a really cool way to kind of click through and view old GeoCities pages.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是一种非常酷的方式，可以让你点击浏览旧的GeoCities页面。

sentences.en: And like there's this theme song that loops around that's been playing in my head for like the last two months.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一首循环播放的主题曲，过去两个月一直在我脑海里回荡。

sentences.en: Like, it's great.
sentences.zh: 真的很棒。

sentences.en: So, you should definitely look at it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你一定要去看看。

sentences.en: Another website that's worth checking out is called DeletedCity.net, which is this awesome like interactive map created by a designer named Richard Vigen,
sentences.zh: 另一个值得一看的网站叫DeletedCity.net，这是一个由设计师Richard Vigen创建的超酷交互式地图，

sentences.en: where you could browse through the GeoCities neighborhoods as if they were like neighborhoods on it, like a city grid.
sentences.zh: 你可以像浏览城市网格一样浏览GeoCities的社区。

sentences.en: So, it's really cool to be able to zoom in and like see it.
sentences.zh: 能够放大查看真的很酷。

sentences.en: Like, if it were an actual city, this is what it would look like.
sentences.zh: 如果它是一个真正的城市，看起来就是这样。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 那很酷。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 那很酷。

sentences.en: But one project that I really want to talk about is called One Terabyte of the Kilobyte Age.
sentences.zh: 但我真正想聊的一个项目叫“千字节时代的万亿字节”。

sentences.en: And it was created by two people named Olia Lialina and Dragan Espenshid.
sentences.zh: 它是由Olia Lialina和Dragan Espenshid两人创建的。

sentences.en: And it's an archive of almost 400,000 GeoCities pages.
sentences.zh: 这是一个包含近40万个GeoCities页面的档案库。

sentences.en: And I originally spoke with Olia for the piece because she had this really interesting relationship with GeoCities and the old web because she was a webmaster and web design professor back in like the mid-90s.
sentences.zh: 我最初为了这期节目采访了Olia，因为她与GeoCities和旧网络有着非常有趣的渊源，她在90年代中期曾是一名站长和网页设计教授。

sentences.en: And she told me that she used to save webpages like the ones in GeoCities so she could show her students examples of like how not to build a good webpage.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她过去常保存像GeoCities那样的网页，这样她就能向学生展示如何“不”去构建一个好网页的例子。

sentences.en: Like, don't use like twinkling star backgrounds or a million different colors or those under construction signs that are never taken off.
sentences.zh: 比如，不要使用闪烁的星星背景，不要使用一百万种不同的颜色，也不要使用那些永远不会被撤下的“施工中”标志。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，没错。

sentences.en: Like, don't do this.
sentences.zh: 比如，别这么做。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: But, you know, she said that she was noticing the shift from, you know, web 1.0 to web 2.0 in real time towards the end of the late 90s and the beginning of the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 但她说，她在90年代末到21世纪初实时注意到了从Web 1.0到Web 2.0的转变。

sentences.en: Because it was getting a lot harder for her to find, like, the twinkling star backgrounds or the welcome to my homepage GIFs.
sentences.zh: 因为她发现越来越难找到那些闪烁的星星背景或“欢迎来到我的主页”的GIF图了。

sentences.en: You mean homepage GIFs?
sentences.zh: 你是说主页GIF？

sentences.en: GIFs.
sentences.zh: 你以前出去的时候吗？

sentences.en: Homepage GIFs.
sentences.zh: 主页GIF。

sentences.en: Like, we're not going to start this right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在可别开始争论这个。

sentences.en: Okay, keep going.
sentences.zh: 好吧，继续。

sentences.en: But, like, you know, because she started seeing that they're, like, disappearing.
sentences.zh: 但因为她开始看到它们在消失，

sentences.en: She really started to study these things and, like, really loved the design of the early web because of what it represented.
sentences.zh: 她真的开始研究这些东西，并且因为它们所代表的意义，而深深爱上了早期网页的设计。

sentences.en: Because of very pragmatic reasons, I started to collect them.
sentences.zh: 出于非常务实的原因，我开始收集它们。

sentences.en: Just, you know, safe graphics.
sentences.zh: 只是，你知道，保存图形。

sentences.en: And it was not because I thought at that time that you should archive the web or it can have some historic significance.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为我当时认为你应该存档网络，或者它有什么历史意义。

sentences.en: But then I realized that it's not just that some funny websites are disappearing, but visions of how the worldwide web should be, they are getting changed.
sentences.zh: 但后来我意识到，不仅仅是一些有趣的网站在消失，而是关于万维网应该是什么样子的愿景，正在发生改变。

sentences.en: So when the Geocities Torrent got released on the Pirate Bay, Olya and Dragan, like, immediately downloaded it and have been studying it ever since.
sentences.zh: 所以当GeoCities的种子文件在海盗湾发布时，Olia和Dragan立即下载了它，并从那时起一直研究至今。

sentences.en: But what I really like about the work that they're doing is that this is not a nostalgic exercise.
sentences.zh: 但我真正喜欢他们工作的一点是，这不仅仅是一种怀旧练习。

sentences.en: They're really looking at what these early web elements can teach us about our relationship with the web in the 90s and early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 他们真正着眼于这些早期网络元素能教会我们关于90年代和21世纪初我们与网络的关系。

sentences.en: Like, if you look at something like the under construction sign, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你看看“施工中”标志之类的东西。

sentences.en: On the construction sign, it's not just a funny picture.
sentences.zh: “施工中”标志不仅仅是一张有趣的图片。

sentences.en: It's not just a symbol for the old website.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是旧网站的象征。

sentences.en: But I try to explain what does it mean exactly?
sentences.zh: 我试着解释它到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: Why is it important?
sentences.zh: 为什么它很重要？

sentences.en: So basically, the under construction sign was a symbol for this moment when the web was being hand built by amateur users.
sentences.zh: 基本上，“施工中”标志象征着那个网络由业余用户亲手构建的时刻。

sentences.en: And there was this general acceptance that a website could be a work in progress.
sentences.zh: 当时人们普遍接受网站可以是一个“进行中”的作品。

sentences.en: Like, you could take your time and it was OK for people to get a glimpse of, like, the building process before it was finished.
sentences.zh: 你可以慢慢来，人们在网站完成之前看到它的构建过程也是可以接受的。

sentences.en: But that all changed with the introduction of Web 2.0 because more professional web designers were taking over and big social networking sites were taking over.
sentences.zh: 但随着Web 2.0的引入，这一切都变了，因为更专业的网页设计师接管了网络，大型社交网站也接管了网络。

sentences.en: On the construction sign was really the first one that professional designers started to remove from the website.
sentences.zh: “施工中”标志确实是专业设计师开始从网站上移除的第一个元素。

sentences.en: Because, oh, well, how can it be that something is not ready?
sentences.zh: 因为，哦，怎么可能有什么东西还没准备好呢？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I never thought about that before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没想过这一点。

sentences.en: Like, the disappearance of the under construction sign really signaled this move towards a kind of corporate version of the Internet.
sentences.zh: “施工中”标志的消失确实标志着向一种企业版互联网的转变。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what Olya believes.
sentences.zh: 是的，Olia就是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And, like, this is just one aspect of how Geocities is being studied.
sentences.zh: 这只是GeoCities被研究的一个方面。

sentences.en: But I thought this was cool because projects like this basically show that it's possible to apply some sort of, like,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这很酷，因为像这样的项目基本上表明，可以将某种，比如，

sentences.en: archaeological lens to this website that a lot of people wrote off as useless.
sentences.zh: 考古学的视角应用到这个被许多人视为无用的网站上。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it totally makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这完全说得通。

sentences.en: I mean, it would tell us what we were thinking at the time, that you needed to put up a site so badly, like, within 10 minutes,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它会告诉我们当时我们在想什么，你急于在10分钟内建立一个网站，

sentences.en: that you had to put an under construction sign on there.
sentences.zh: 以至于你不得不放上一个“施工中”标志。

sentences.en: But you might take it with it or you might just leave it, you know?
sentences.zh: 但你可能会带着它，或者你可能只是把它留在那里，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Who cares?

sentences.zh: 那个即将终结的世界叫《模拟人生在线》。

sentences.en: You've all been wonderful.

sentences.en: You've helped me through a hard time in my life when I first got online.

sentences.en: But ironically, the online version of The Sims was not very popular.

sentences.en: Thank you.

sentences.en: As you can probably hear, EA Land is not a normal video game.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能听到的，EA Land不是一款普通的游戏。

sentences.en: There were no monsters, no killing.
sentences.zh: 没有怪物，没有杀戮。

sentences.en: And although it had some competitive elements, for many players, competition wasn't the point at all.
sentences.zh: 虽然它有一些竞争元素，但对许多玩家来说，竞争根本不是重点。

sentences.en: Unlike a lot of other games where you might be shooting people or slaying dragons or something, this was a game about socializing.

sentences.en: That's Robert Ashley.

sentences.en: It was a nice place.
sentences.zh: 那是一个不错的地方。

sentences.en: Where everyone knows your name.

sentences.en: My wife had a long-term illness from a blood transfusion.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子因输血患上了长期疾病。

sentences.en: She had hepatitis C.
sentences.zh: 她得了丙型肝炎。

sentences.en: And the last three years or so of her life were pretty much a challenge for both of us.
sentences.zh: 她生命中最后三年左右的时间，对我们俩来说都是相当大的挑战。

sentences.en: And after she passed away, I had absolutely no function other than to wake up, go to work, and go to sleep again.
sentences.zh: 她去世后，我除了起床、上班、睡觉，完全没有任何生活动力。

sentences.en: And with her illness, I didn't get out and socialize much.
sentences.zh: 因为她的病，我很少出门社交。

sentences.en: We, you know, we weren't able to, you know, go out to the bars and meet up with friends and have dinner.

sentences.en: I totally de-socialized myself.
sentences.zh: 我彻底切断了社交。

sentences.en: And this game was kind of a way for me to just kind of get back into living again.
sentences.zh: 而这款游戏成了我重新回归生活的一种方式。

sentences.en: It was pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真的很神奇。

sentences.en: And Paul began to live for EA Land.

sentences.en: It was the first thing he did when he got home from work.

sentences.en: You're treated to a big, warm greeting.

sentences.en: And you'd be imitated with that.

sentences.en: It made you feel really good.

sentences.en: It wasn't the real world.

sentences.en: But his friends were real friends.

sentences.en: And virtual worlds do have an upside.

sentences.en: Your race, your color, your religion, all that can be totally masked.
sentences.zh: 你的种族、肤色、宗教信仰，所有这些都可以被完全掩盖。

sentences.en: And you're truly judged on who you really are and how you present yourself.
sentences.zh: 你真正被评价的是你的本质以及你如何展现自己。

sentences.en: There's no prejudice.
sentences.zh: 没有偏见。

sentences.en: There's no preconceived anything.
sentences.zh: 没有任何先入为主的观念。

sentences.en: It's just, you're really taken at face value.
sentences.zh: 你只是被真实地看待。

sentences.en: People could really, like, break loose and be themselves and have some fun.
sentences.zh: 人们真的可以释放自我，做回自己，享受乐趣。

sentences.en: It just feels really good.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉真的很好。

sentences.en: But Paul's utopia didn't last because EA Land started hemorrhaging money.
sentences.zh: 但保罗的乌托邦没能持续下去，因为EA Land开始入不敷出。

sentences.en: The writing was on the wall.
sentences.zh: 大势已去。

sentences.en: The server was about to go dark.
sentences.zh: 服务器即将关闭。

sentences.en: And this event, this virtual apocalypse, might only exist in the memory of the players.
sentences.zh: 而这场虚拟世界的末日，或许只会存在于玩家的记忆中。

sentences.en: If it weren't for Dr. Henry Lowood.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为亨利·洛伍德（Henry Lowood）博士的话。

sentences.en: I had just stumbled across this project by Henry Lowood.
sentences.zh: 我当时偶然发现了亨利·洛伍德的这个项目。

sentences.en: My name is Henry Lowood.
sentences.zh: 我叫亨利·洛伍德。

sentences.en: Who is this archival researcher at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 他是斯坦福大学的一位档案研究员。

sentences.en: And I had a project called How They Got Game, which is on the history of digital games and simulations.
sentences.zh: 我当时有一个名为“他们如何获得游戏”（How They Got Game）的项目，研究的是数字游戏和模拟的历史。

sentences.en: Saving video games for future generations.
sentences.zh: 为后代保存电子游戏。

sentences.en: You know, 50, 100, 200 years from now.
How are we going to save that history?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何保存那段历史？

sentences.en: You know, like, we've got to save the video games.
sentences.zh: 我们必须保存这些电子游戏。

sentences.en: So Dr. Lowood and his colleagues preserve what happens inside video games.
sentences.zh: 所以洛伍德博士和他的同事们致力于保存电子游戏内部发生的一切。

sentences.en: Now, for a single-player game like Pac-Man, for example, this is easy.
sentences.zh: 对于像《吃豆人》这样的单机游戏，这很容易。

sentences.en: You effectively take out the Atari cartridge and put it on the shelf.
sentences.zh: 你只需取出雅达利卡带，把它放在架子上就行了。

sentences.en: But saving multiplayer online games is not so simple.
sentences.zh: 但保存多人在线游戏就没那么简单了。

sentences.en: Saving the software alone is kind of a barren exercise.
sentences.zh: 仅仅保存软件本身是一项毫无意义的工作。

sentences.en: If you save the code for EA Land and turn it on 100 years from now,
sentences.zh: 如果你保存了EA Land的代码，并在100年后运行它，

sentences.en: you'd enter a world and nothing would be there.
sentences.zh: 你会进入一个空无一物的世界。

sentences.en: All the things that Paul Monaco and his friends love would be impossible to find.
sentences.zh: 保罗·摩纳哥和他的朋友们所热爱的一切都将无迹可寻。

sentences.en: You need to document what people are doing in these spaces.
sentences.zh: 你需要记录人们在这些空间里所做的事情。

sentences.en: That situation is much more like what a historian or an archivist would do
sentences.zh: 这种情况更像是历史学家或档案管理员在面对

sentences.en: when faced with the problem of documenting the real world.
sentences.zh: 记录现实世界的问题时所做的工作。

sentences.en: So when Dr. Lowood caught wind of EA Land shutting down,
sentences.zh: 所以当洛伍德博士听到EA Land即将关闭的消息时，

sentences.zh: 他有机会记录下历史学家或考古学家

sentences.zh: 录像带在转动，EA Land最后几个小时的画面被记录下来，

sentences.zh: 最忠实的铁杆用户们在那里交换虚拟拥抱并回忆往事。

sentences.zh: 玩家们打出的信息像漫画里的对话气泡一样出现。

sentences.zh: 你能听到所有化身的哭泣声。
